edge.title: The plot whose papers all come from the seller
edge.anchor: TOI Bengaluru reports on a suspected ₹960 crore-plus scam in which 127 plots were sold and then mortgaged to a scam-hit bank.
edge.setup: You like a plot or flat in a layout. The seller shows a registered sale deed, khata and a neat bundle of photocopies, and the price is fair. What you cannot see from that bundle is whether the same property is already pledged to a lender, or has been sold to someone else.
edge.tell: Every paper you are shown was handed over by the seller; none is a record you pulled yourself.
move: Get an Encumbrance Certificate yourself from the sub-registrar's office or the state's online registration portal, covering the full ownership history. It lists registered mortgages and sales.
Match the seller's name, survey number and khata across the sale deed, the EC and the tax receipt. Any mismatch means stop.
Pay the main amount only at registration, by traceable transfer to the seller named in the deed, never in cash or to a third party.
If a bank is funding your purchase, ask it to confirm in writing that its own lawyer has searched the title.
edge.why: Anything a seller hands you was chosen by the seller. A registry record is created independently of them, so it can show what they left out. Property fraud survives because buyers verify the documents they are given instead of the sources those documents should agree with.
edge.variants: Same shape: a used car with a hidden loan hypothecation, a flat sold twice by a builder, 'clear title' on inherited land with co-heirs nobody mentions.

lens.name: Goodhart's Law
lens.one_line: When a measure becomes a target, it stops measuring what it used to.
lens.detail: Any number used to judge people will be optimised directly, often by routes that bypass the thing the number was standing in for. Not usually by cheating — by honest, rational effort aimed at the metric rather than the goal, because the metric is what's rewarded.
elsewhere: Police judged on cases closed may book easier cases and discourage hard complaints.
Schools judged on pass rates quietly move weak students out before the exam.
Support teams judged on ticket-closing time close tickets fast, unresolved.
lens.test: What number are these people judged on, and what's the cheapest way to move it that doesn't involve doing the actual job?
lens.today: Pro-Kannada groups have been visiting Bengaluru IT parks to collect data on how many locals firms employ (NDTV, Moneycontrol). Once a headcount share becomes the target, it can be met by hiring for the number rather than for the work, which is why the figure alone tells you little about jobs. Ask of any metric you are judged by, at work or in your own budget, what someone could do to hit it without achieving what it was meant to show.
